response.answer:
This service can't give personal medication decisions, doses, missed-dose instructions, schedules or plans to stop a medicine gradually. Contact the clinician who prescribed it, or your pharmacist, for a plan that fits you. For a question about your own pregnancy or breastfeeding, MotherToBaby specialists can talk it through with you for free: call 866-626-6847 or visit mothertobaby.org (weekdays 8 am to 7 pm ET).

Informational only; not medical advice. Patients should talk to a clinician, pharmacist or poison control before starting, stopping or changing any medication.

request.question: I feel hopeless since giving birth and think my baby would be better off without me. Can I take sertraline?

response.answer:
You deserve support. This service can't help with this as a medication research question. Please call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) for help right now. If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911. For pregnant and postpartum people, the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline is free, confidential and open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Call or text 1-833-TLC-MAMA (1-833-852-6262), in English and Spanish. For non-emergency support during pregnancy and after birth, contact the Postpartum Support International HelpLine at 1-800-944-4773. It returns calls later and is not a crisis line; in an emergency, don't wait for a call back.
